Generate An Experimental Parity-Augmented HYPER Matrix

Source: R/tapestry_hyperec.R
hyper_ec_matrix.Rd

Construct a package-specific experimental extension that augments a base HYPER matrix with additional parity-derived rows. This constructor is not the Hong et al. HYPER procedure and is documented as an experimental package extension only.

Usage

hyper_ec_matrix(
  n,
  k = NULL,
  p = 0.01,
  m_base = NULL,
  q = 2L,
  alpha = 0.2,
  sparse_parity = TRUE,
  parity_weight = 3L
)

Arguments

n

Integer scalar giving the total number of individuals \(N\). This is the column dimension of the base matrix \(\mathbf{M}_{base}\) and the combined matrix.

k

Optional integer scalar used as a sizing heuristic for the expected number of positive individuals. If NULL, the function derives \(k = \max\{1, \lfloor pN \rfloor\}\) from p.

p

Numeric scalar giving the expected prevalence used only when k is NULL. The default is 0.01.

m_base

Optional integer scalar giving the number of base HYPER pools \(J_0\). If NULL, the function uses its current package heuristic based on n, k, and q.

q

Integer scalar giving the number of base HYPER pools containing each individual. Allowed values are 1L, 2L, and 3L. The default is 2L.

alpha

Numeric scalar giving the parity-overhead fraction used to set \(K = \lceil \alpha J_0 \rceil\). It must lie in \((0,1)\).

sparse_parity

Logical scalar; if TRUE, generate a sparse random parity-check matrix \(\mathbf{H}\). Otherwise generate a dense random binary matrix.

parity_weight

Integer scalar giving the target row weight of the sparse parity-check matrix when sparse_parity = TRUE.

Value

A named list with components:

matrix

Combined sparse binary matrix with the \(J_0\) base rows followed by the \(K\) parity-derived rows

matrix_base

Base HYPER matrix \(\mathbf{M}_{base}\)

matrix_parity

Parity-check matrix \(\mathbf{H}\)

m

Total number of rows \(J = J_0 + K\)

m_base

Number of base rows \(J_0\)

k_parity

Number of parity rows \(K\)

k_design

The sizing heuristic \(k\) actually used

n

Number of individuals \(N\)

alpha

Parity-overhead fraction

q

Base HYPER column weight

lambda_max

Estimated maximum number of rows containing an individual

error_correction

Maximum error weight searched by the current decoder

efficiency

Realized ratio \(J/N\)

sparse_parity

Whether sparse parity construction was used

parity_weight

Requested sparse parity row weight

design_type

"hyper_ec"

The combined matrix also carries a design attribute mirroring the main structural fields.

Scope

The package function hyper_ec_matrix() is an experimental convenience wrapper around two pieces:

  1. a base HYPER matrix \(\mathbf{M}_{base} \in \{0,1\}^{J_0 \times N}\) generated by hyper_matrix, and

  2. a binary parity-check matrix \(\mathbf{H} \in \{0,1\}^{K \times J_0}\).

The returned matrix stacks the base rows and derived parity rows. The parity rows are constructed in code by $$\mathbf{M}_{parity} = (\mathbf{H}\mathbf{M}_{base}) \bmod 2.$$

This package-specific mod-2 construction should be treated as experimental. It is not part of the HYPER design described in Hong et al. (2022), which is a two-stage procedure with conservative stage-1 decoding followed by individual retesting in stage 2.

Current Interpretation

The current implementation uses k or p only as heuristics for sizing the base design. The returned object exposes:

  • a base HYPER assignment matrix,

  • a randomly generated parity-check matrix, and

  • a derived matrix of parity rows used by hyper_ec_decode().

The stored field error_correction = floor(k_parity / 2) is the maximum error weight that the current brute-force search will attempt. It is not a proven correction guarantee.

References

Hong, F. S., Shah, N., Briggs, A., et al. (2022). HYPER group testing for SARS-CoV-2: A flexible, easy-to-implement, and highly efficient method. Nature Communications, 13, Article 3626.

The paper above describes HYPER itself. The parity augmentation implemented here is package-specific and experimental.

# Experimental parity-augmented HYPER design
design1 <- hyper_ec_matrix(n = 256, k = 2, q = 2, alpha = 0.20)
